flags.title: The three estimates are owner-supplied quotes; no official source can confirm a private quote
flags.detail: E-01 ($614), E-02 ($550) and E-03 ($135) are quotations the project owner received on 2026-08-30. No public or official register records what a contractor quotes privately, so these amounts are published in a column headed 'Quoted amount (owner-supplied)' and the separate official-confirmation field is left blank for all three rows. Nothing was inferred, rounded or adjusted. The provider names were matched to licensed entities by name + San Francisco address + classification; the owner must confirm they are the same businesses he contacted.

flags.title: The three quotes describe different scopes and are not directly comparable
flags.detail: E-03 ($135) is 'repair or adjust plunger handle'; E-02 ($550) is 'replace lever for the bathtub plug and spout with diverter, labor and materials'; E-01 ($614) is 'replacing waste and overflow' (full assembly). None of the three quotes explicitly includes drywall opening or ceiling restoration, which the fallback approach (working from below through a storage-unit ceiling) will likely require (R-06, R-07). Third-party guides put drywall patching at $300–$930 on top of plumbing work.

flags.title: CSLB statuses are point-in-time (all 13 rows re-verified 2026-11-07)
flags.detail: All 13 licence rows were re-read line by line on the official CSLB licence-detail pages on 2026-11-07 and matched this site's data (status, classification, entity, issue/expiry dates, address of record, phone, bond and workers' comp). CSLB states that status can change at any time and that its database may lag, so re-check each linked page before contracting. Four licences are workers'-compensation exempt (certified no employees): Bay Area Plumbing #757796, Save-On-Interior #749536, SF Building Group #1106131 and Rapid Flow #1115649. Fast Response's policy #1024971 expires 2026-12-18; Heise's #1089561 expires 2027-01-11; Discount #1140843 carries $2,000,000 liability cover to 2027-04-01.

flags.title: No provider in the set holds a C-9 Drywall classification
flags.detail: None of the verified licenses includes C-9 (Drywall). The all-in-one requirement (R-07) is therefore satisfiable in two CSLB-sanctioned ways: (a) hire a B-licensed general contractor who contracts both the C-36 plumbing and a licensed C-9 drywall subcontractor under one contract (Ace #829071 and We Do Construction #1096552 hold B + C-36; SF Building Group #1106131 holds B), or (b) hire a C-36 plumber and separately contract a licensed drywall contractor. CSLB's official guidance: a B contractor is appropriate when a job requires more than two types of work and cannot legally contract for a single trade only.

source_links.label: CSLB — Find A Licensed Contractor (B vs C multi-trade guidance)

flags.title: Access-panel code section numbering differs across CPC editions
flags.detail: The 12-inch access requirement for concealed slip-joint connections (directly relevant to tub waste/overflow serviceability) is numbered 402.10 in the 2022 California Plumbing Code / UPC, but 404.2 in the 2010 CPC. Links to both editions are provided; the requirement text itself is consistent.

flags.title: Fast Response Plumbing & Rooter: CSLB address differs from website address
flags.detail: CSLB record of record for license #1024971 lists 236 W Portal Ave #459, San Francisco 94127; the company website displays 4444 Geary Blvd Ste 203, San Francisco 94118. Same license number and phone on both. Likely a mailing/office address difference; confirm at contract time.

flags.title: Review counts unknown for We Do Construction, SF Building Group, and Rapid Flow
flags.detail: No review counts or ratings could be captured for these three providers from the sources fetched this session. Per the verification rule, those cells are left blank rather than estimated. Ask both for references from occupied-unit jobs.

flags.title: Photos of the work area not yet available
flags.detail: The project owner states reference photos will be provided later; all analysis in this session is based on the written description only (R-12). Site access, tub type (alcove/freestanding), finish (tile/surround), and the storage-unit ceiling construction are unconfirmed and materially affect scope.

flags.title: Advanced Plumbing and Drain (#1009195): CSLB 'may be suspended at a future date' warning
flags.detail: The official CSLB record for license #1009195 (verified 2026-11-06) carries an Additional Status: 'The license may be suspended at a future date for failure to resolve an outstanding final liability from the Franchise Tax Board, Department of Industrial Relations, Employment Development Department, or the Contractors State License Board.' The license is currently active. Re-check the CSLB page immediately before any engagement.

flags.title: Duplicate public briefs from parallel sessions are retired to redirects
flags.detail: Earlier parallel sessions published their own copies of this brief at /bathtub/, /bathtub-overflow/, /bathroom-overflow/, /trip-lever/ and /docs/bathtub-*.html. Those routes now open a redirect page that forwards to the corresponding page of this canonical site, so no old URL breaks and only one authoritative copy is browsable. The retired pages and their data files remain in the repository history and on disk; their unique verified findings (Save-On-Interior #749536 and Ayoob & Peery #392967) were re-verified and carried into the canonical provider table.

flags.title: CSLB spells the street name on Fast Response's record as 'POTRAL'
flags.detail: The official CSLB record for #1024971 (re-read 2026-11-07) gives the address of record as '236 W POTRAL AVE #459, San Francisco, CA 94127'. That is a spelling error in the CSLB database, reproduced here rather than silently corrected. The company's own site shows a different address (4444 Geary Blvd Ste 203 — F-08), which is why the two must not be blended.

flags.title: No written confirmation from any provider that the lever can be removed from above
flags.detail: The brief reports that five or more licensed plumbers could not remove the assembly from above without risking the hidden plumbing, but no provider has put that in writing and no provider has quoted the below-floor plumbing-plus-drywall scope as one itemised job. Until that exists, both the 'from above' and the 'from below' path remain options rather than decisions.

flags.title: Cost benchmarks are third-party guide figures, not official prices
flags.detail: The published ranges ($200–$1,025 for tub drain work; $300–$930 for drywall patching) come from 2026 consumer cost guides (HomeGuide, Angi). They are labelled as third-party and are not treated as verified; no government or licensing body publishes repair prices, and the money rows in the executive summary therefore show 'unverified'.
